turns.text: ok just got back from my run on the marsh boardwalk, need info for a project. ops management group project, we're modeling ridgeline-style tote flow, due nov 20. pls explain how hiring fairs like th ridgeline one affect warehouse staffing. tldr style

Tote-flow project, good topic. Here's the short version of how a seasonal hiring fair affects warehouse staffing:

- **Capacity ramp:** Mass hiring adds labor ahead of peak volume, so throughput capacity rises in steps as each cohort finishes onboarding.
- **Onboarding lag:** New hires take 1-3 weeks to reach full pick rate, so effective capacity is lower than headcount suggests.
- **Productivity mix:** Experienced and new pickers run at different rates, so model two or more labor classes.
- **Training load:** Veterans spend time training, which dips their own output.
- **Attrition:** Seasonal turnover is high, so you need over-hiring buffers.
- **Shift coverage:** Fairs often fill specific shifts, usually nights and weekends, which shifts where bottlenecks form.
- **Cost tradeoff:** Hiring too early burns payroll; too late means missed ship windows and overtime.

For your model, useful inputs: hires per cohort, ramp curve, attrition rate, and picks per hour by labor class. Want this as a table?

yes table pls. also lowkey useful, heard from around th complex that aaliyah got hired at th ridgeline fair, and i was talking w my roommate marcus about it, he works there so he said th ramp thing is real

Sounds like you've got a good firsthand source in your roommate. Here's the table:

| Factor | Effect on staffing | Model input |
|---|---|---|
| Cohort hiring | Step increases in headcount | Hires per cohort, start dates |
| Onboarding ramp | New hires below full rate for 1-3 weeks | Ramp curve (e.g., 50%, 75%, 100%) |
| Labor classes | Veterans vs. new hires differ in rate | Picks/hour per class |
| Training drag | Veteran output dips while mentoring | Hours diverted per new hire |
| Attrition | Seasonal churn erodes gains | Weekly attrition % |
| Shift mix | Fair hires concentrate on certain shifts | Headcount per shift |
| Cost vs. service | Early hiring costs payroll, late hiring risks missed ships | Labor cost/hr vs. late-ship penalty |

Since your roommate works there, ask him for real numbers: how long new pickers take to hit rate, and how scanner quotas are set. Even rough figures make a stronger model. Just cite them as informal anecdotal inputs unless you can verify them.
